newsitem.title: USA: Cohen asks bipartisan support on defense policy.
newsitem.headline: Cohen asks bipartisan support on defense policy.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary nominee William Cohen urged the Republican-controlled Congress on Wednesday to give Democratic President Bill Clinton bipartisan support in maintaining U.S. world leadership and promised to give personal emphasis to Asia and the Pacific.

"I intend to give new focus to our security relations in the Asia-Pacific region," the retired Republican senator from Maine told the Senate Armed Services Committee at the opening of his confirmation hearing.

Cohen, expected to be quickly confirmed by the Senate as the first Republican in Clinton's Cabinet, said his nomination was "a clear signal" of the president's commitment to the principle that the security of the nation should not be a partisan matter.

He said bipartisanship was absolutely necessary in facing the challenges posed by problems in Russia and other emerging democracies in Europe as well as regional problems in East Asia and Southwest Asia.

"As the centre of gravity of the world economy has shifted to the Pacific, our increasing economic integration with Asia's dynamic economies has created enormous opportunities for American businessmen and workers," he said.

"While there always will be room for legitimate debate on national security issues, partisanship and parochialism should occupy no seat at the table of out deliberations," said Cohen, who gained a reputation as a moderate, consensus-builder in 24 years in Congress.
